headline: Strongest and most consistently supported predictive relationship in the interpretability analysis.
quantitative_evidence: Individual permutation: ROC-AUC decrease = 0.049161, AP decrease = 0.050338; coherent PDP: 0.088177 at 0 prior inpatient encounters to 0.245096 at 5.
interpretation: The locked model assigns progressively higher estimated readmission probability as prior inpatient utilization increases across the primary supported range.
caveat: Predictive association only; correlated utilization representations prevent additive attribution.

headline: Strongest engineered diagnosis representation with support-stable categorical behavior.
quantitative_evidence: Individual permutation: ROC-AUC decrease = 0.011278, AP decrease = 0.009883; profile range = 0.021906 and remained 0.021906 at ≥500 encounters/category.
interpretation: Broad primary diagnosis family provides meaningful information to the locked prediction function.
caveat: No raw-ICD counterfactual model was fitted, so superiority over raw diagnosis codes is not established.

headline: Substantial individual predictive dependence with nonlinear model behavior.
quantitative_evidence: Individual permutation: ROC-AUC decrease = 0.013746, AP decrease = 0.006102; PDP range = 0.027051 with maximum average prediction around 8 days.
interpretation: Length of stay contributes meaningful predictive information, with a nonlinear fitted response.
caveat: Upper-tail decline requires caution and is not evidence that changing length of stay changes readmission risk.

headline: Moderate individual magnitude but highly coherent model-behavior evidence.
quantitative_evidence: Individual permutation: ROC-AUC decrease = 0.003982; PDP increased from 0.091916 to 0.113366 over the supported 1–9 range.
interpretation: The model associates greater documented diagnostic complexity with higher estimated readmission probability.
caveat: Diagnosis count may reflect coding/documentation intensity as well as clinical complexity.

headline: Engineered features showed heterogeneous value rather than uniformly improving interpretation.
quantitative_evidence: prior_utilization_total ROC-AUC permutation decrease = 0.005011; four log1p utilization features had zero measurable individual ROC-AUC and AP permutation importance.
interpretation: The engineered utilization total contributes measurable signal, while the log transformations appear redundant within this locked HGB representation.
caveat: Zero individual importance does not imply universal uselessness in other algorithms or datasets.

headline: Empirical-support checks materially changed the interpretation of several categorical effects.
quantitative_evidence: diag_2_family profile range contracted from 0.034268 to 0.008737 at ≥500 encounters/category; age and medical specialty also showed support sensitivity.
interpretation: Sparse-category extremes should not be presented as equally stable model behavior.
caveat: Categorical perturbation profiles are fitted-model responses, not subgroup causal effects.

headline: Predictive dependence, model behavior, support, and causal claims were kept explicitly separate.
quantitative_evidence: Nine prespecified findings were triangulated across individual importance, grouped importance, model behavior, and empirical support.
interpretation: Interpretability conclusions were based on converging evidence rather than a single feature-importance ranking.
caveat: Development-validation interpretation does not establish external validity, deployment readiness, or causal effects.
